thesis: Priced like propane is on its last legs: at C$6.71 the stock only works if cash flow shrinks about 1% a year forever. Certarus trucks gas to data centres that can't wait for a pipeline, and signed contracts drive volume growth in 2027-28 as debt falls toward 3x.
context: My first call in my chosen coverage area, built on a full source process: AIF, MD&A, earnings call Q&A, investor presentations, consensus and news flow. Shaped by coffee chats with equity research analysts: lead with a view that differs from the market, name the catalysts, and keep it short.

thesis: Durable, contracted cash flows, but C$105B of debt and a premium multiple absorb too much value before it reaches common equity. Even the bull case sits below the price at the valuation date.
context: Written after an equity research analyst advised me to keep reports short. The aim was to lead with a view and keep only what drives value. The trade-off: the thesis and catalysts are there, but the 3-page format gave them too little room.

thesis: A dominant franchise with a deep software moat, but the price already reflects most of the Blackwell cycle. A deliberately conservative DCF leaves room to be proven wrong on the upside.
context: My first full report, written to see whether I could apply what I'd learned in school: a three-statement forecast, DCF, comps and scenarios built from scratch. Heavy on the model, light on industry context and primary sources.
